text.p: Fruehauf Trailer Corp said Friday that Derek Nagle, executive vice president of North American operations, was named president of the company.
Nagle will assume most of the responsibilities previously held by Thomas Roller, the former president and chief executive officer, it added.
On August 20, Fruehauf said Roller resigned to become the president and chief executive officer of Wolverine Tube Inc.

The company, which makes truck trailers, also said Timothy Wiggins, executive vice president and chief financial officer, resigned to accept a new position. Wiggins' resignation will become effective on September 15, it added.

Fruehauf also said its board of directors formed a special committee to coordinate the implementation of a previously announced strategic plan. Richard Nevins, a director of the company since January 1995, will chair that committee.
Earlier this month, Fruehauf said it was pursuing the sale of one or more business units, or the entire company.

For the second quarter, Fruehauf posted income of $5.7 million or $0.15 a share, including a $14 million gain on the sale of overseas assets. Excluding the sales, it would have had a net loss of $8.2 million or $0.21 a share.
Commenting on his appointment, Nagle said, "My focus will continue to be primarily directed to the company's operations."
